transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Well... I guess I'm just having trouble keeping my mind on one thing anymore. 

It's just... if a saw starts up in the shop, or somebody walks past, or I even just think about another job... I get pulled off what I'm doing. And then the whole day just kind of gets away from me. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you always had trouble focusing like this, even back when you were in school? Or is this something that's gotten worse more recently?

I suppose it's always been there. Even back in grade school... before I was 12, I guess. Teachers were always telling my mother I was... well, bright, but careless. I was always losing my homework, or... forgetting instructions. Just staring out the window instead of finishing my seatwork. So... it's not really new.
Besides having trouble focusing, do you find yourself feeling restless or fidgety? Like, do you have trouble sitting still, or do you feel like you need to be moving around?

Well... I don't know about restless, exactly. 

I just... if I have to sit at the desk doing estimates, or if I'm stuck in a long meeting... I get this feeling inside. Like I'm all wound up. I just feel like I need to get up and move around. Even though my wrist is healed up now and I know I'm supposed to just stay put and finish what I'm doing. It's just... hard to stay in one spot for too long.
When you were in school as a kid, did teachers or your parents ever say you were hyperactive, or that you were always running around, talking a lot, or having trouble waiting your turn?
No... I don't think so. I wasn't really a loud kid. Just... quiet, mostly. Nobody ever said I was bouncing off the walls or anything like that.
When you were in school, did your trouble with focusing and attention happen in most of your classes, or was it mainly in certain subjects or situations?

I don't really know... that was a long time ago. 

I guess it was just... most of them? I don't remember it being just one subject or anything. It was just... hard to pay attention in general, I suppose.
When you were a kid in school, did you ever have trouble with things like interrupting people, blurting things out, or acting without thinking first?
No... not really. Like I said before, I kept to myself mostly. I wasn't the type to... just blurt things out or interrupt people. I usually just stayed quiet.

You mentioned trouble with focus at work and back in school. How has this affected you overall—like, has it caused problems with your job performance, relationships, or other important areas of your life?

I suppose... yeah. It's caused some issues. 

At work... I've had to redo things on jobs because of mistakes. It's cost me some commissions. The crew doesn't really rely on me for scheduling or ordering materials anymore... just because of the delays. 

And at home... my husband just takes care of the bills and reminders now. I kept misplacing the papers, or just... missing what needed to be done. So he took over.

When you were a kid, did you have trouble sitting still in class or at home? Like, were you always moving around, swinging your legs, fidgeting with things, or did adults tell you to sit down and be still?
No... not really. I think I just... sat there, mostly. I don't remember anyone having to tell me to be still or anything.

You mentioned having trouble focusing since before age 12. Looking back, would you say you had these attention problems at home as well as at school, or was it mainly something that happened at school?
I guess... it was everywhere. At school, yeah. But at home, too. Just... always sort of in my own world, I suppose.

When you were a child, did anyone ever describe you as daydreaming a lot, or say that you seemed to be in your own world? Or did they notice you were slow to get started on things, or that you seemed kind of sluggish or unmotivated?
I don't really know. It's been a long time. I don't remember anyone using those words, or... calling me sluggish or anything. I just kind of kept to myself, I guess.

You mentioned feeling wound up and needing to move around during long meetings or desk work. When you were younger in school, did you ever have problems like that—needing to get up and move, or feeling restless during class?
I don't think so. I... I just sat there. I don't remember needing to move around or anything back then.

When you were trying to focus on something back in school—like reading a textbook or doing math problems—was it that you couldn't keep your attention on it even when you tried hard? Or was it more that you just didn't feel like putting in the effort, or didn't care much about it?

I couldn't really tell you. It was a long time ago. I just know the work didn't get done. I don't really remember what was going through my head back then, or... if I was trying or not. I just couldn't do it.

You mentioned that as an adult, you feel wound up and need to move around during desk work. But when you think back to your teenage years—say, when you were 13 to 18—do you remember having that same restless, wound-up feeling back then, or is that something that's more recent?
I'm not sure... I don't think I felt like that as a teenager. I don't really remember being restless back then. It's... probably just a more recent thing, I guess.

When you were in your 20s and 30s, before this wound-up feeling started, were you able to sit through long meetings or desk work without that restless feeling? Or has it always been like this for you?

I don't really know. I mean... I've always worked with my hands, mostly. Being a carpenter, you're always moving anyway. So... sitting at a desk wasn't really something I had to do much back then. I just... I don't remember it being an issue.

When you do have to sit and do desk work now—like with the estimates—is this wound-up, restless feeling something that's been getting worse over time, or has it pretty much stayed the same since you first started having to do more desk work?

I guess it's... pretty much stayed the same. It's been going on for about a year and a month now. That's when I broke my wrist... and they shifted me off the tools. Put me on shop paperwork and supervising instead. So... yeah. Just since then.

Before you broke your wrist and had to start doing desk work, did you ever have jobs or situations where you had to sit still for long periods? And if so, did you notice that wound-up, restless feeling back then?

No... not really. I've been doing carpentry pretty much since I got out of school. Never really had a desk job before this. So... I don't know. I didn't really have to sit still for long, so I couldn't tell you.

Back when you were doing carpentry full-time, before the wrist injury, did you ever have trouble paying attention or focusing on things in your everyday life—like conversations, instructions from your boss, or even just remembering to do errands or appointments? Or was the attention problem mainly just something that showed up when you had to sit and do paperwork?

I mean... I guess it wasn't just the paperwork. It's... always been there, really. Even when I was a kid. Before I was 12, I think. My teachers used to tell my mom I was... careless. Losing my homework, forgetting what they told me to do. I'd just sit there and look out the window instead of doing my work. So... yeah. It's not new.
